correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and quantifiers are explicit. Stewart–Sierpiński gives a necessary and sufficient local prime-extension criterion. With at most three excluded primes, q2≤13, q3≤17, and for j≥3 Bertrand gives q_{j+1}<16q_j<A_j≤sigma(A_j)+1. Fixed-modulus prime number theorem gives a fresh prime in every required reduced class between X_j/2 and X_j, where X_j/2 exceeds the backbone largest prime, so products stay squarefree and practical. At modulus 5005 every third prime would be one of 5,7,11,13. The least four-prime product proves sharpness; 16680 finite greedy steps and direct tests are supplemental.

value.rationale: The sharp first modulus where squarefree practical unit-class infinitude fails is a motivated natural invariant refining an established arithmetic-progression classification. The proof covers every unit residue for all smaller coprime moduli, yields a uniform three-excluded-prime structural theorem, and shows the contrast between infinitely many unrestricted practical numbers and only three squarefree practical numbers at modulus 5005. This is a complete natural threshold, not an arbitrary finite slice.
